Comments: Two FT-240-43 cores stacked for 160M low-freq headroom. Tightly wound, bifilar preferred for impedance symmetry.
Single FT-240-43 adequate for 80M and up. Common CM choke configuration. Works 80-10M with compromise.
Ten turns optimized for 40M-10M coverage. Reduced turns from 80M improves high-freq response.
Nine turns balances 30M-10M bands. Approaching FT-140-43 territory for weight saving.
Smaller core sufficient for 20M and above. RG-174 (thinner coax) fits better on FT-140.
Seven turns on FT-140-43 provides excellent 17M-10M coverage. Compact, lighter than FT-240.
Same configuration as 17M (broad multi-band design). Alternative: 6 turns for 15M-10M only.
Six turns on FT-140-43 for 12M-10M bands. Very compact form factor.
Six turns optimized for 10M+6M coverage (see below for 6M). Minimal size/weight.
FT-240-61 (lower permeability) essential for 6M. Mix 43 loses efficiency at VHF. Five turns adequate CM impedance.
Four turns on FT-240-61 for 2M. Approaching air-core choke territory. Alternative: 8-turn air-core on 3.5-inch form.
Transition to air-core coax choke (ferrite too lossy at UHF). Eight turns on 4-inch diameter PVC pipe.
Standard air-core coax choke. Eight turns on 3.5-inch diameter. Minimal insertion loss (<0.2dB).
Six turns on 3-inch diameter form. Common in UHF repeater/mobile installations.
Five turns on 2.5-inch form for 20cm coverage. Minimal CM suppression at 1.3GHz; primarily passes RF with minimal loss.
